The factsheet does not specify which weight variables (e.g., student design weights or replicate weights) were applied in the production of the reported percentages and mean scores. Analysts using the OECD PISA 2022 microdata should apply the provided student/sampling weights and replicate weights when estimating means, score differences, and proficiency-level distributions; plausible values for the financial literacy scale should be handled according to the OECD PISA scaling methodology.

data.outcome_summary: PISA 2022 is administered to 15-year-old students and assesses key knowledge and skills; in 2022 it measured financial literacy for the fourth time (2012, 2015, 2018, 2022). The Brazil factsheet reports average financial literacy performance (416 points) relative to the OECD average, and the distribution of students across proficiency levels (e.g., 45% below Level 2 and 2% at Level 5). It also summarises how much variation in financial literacy is associated with performance in mathematics and reading (77% explained by these domains, 23% by other domain-specific factors). The factsheet further provides descriptive associations between financial literacy and student characteristics, saving and price-comparison behaviours, parental discussions, and exposure to personal finance tasks at school. Because this is a summary factsheet, it does not provide the underlying model specifications, ML methods, or replication details for weights, plausible-values combining rules, or missing-data handling.
